goal: Release pylemma, a small trust game with ten-round matches against deterministic opponents, real model decisions, stored replays, reviewed public Logfire traces, bounded hosted operation, and a local Logfire example. Complete all six development rounds and the release criteria in SPEC.md.

tasks.title: Establish an installable project with offline checks
tasks.details: Implement SPEC.md sections 3, 7, 16, and phase 0. Create AGENTS.md, a minimal Python package, pyproject.toml, locked dependencies, and installation instructions. Define executable test, formatting, and type-check commands. Document context boundaries and the term list in docs/architecture.md. Verify installation and offline checks from a clean environment. Require factual development records, relevant tests, updated documentation, and simplicity reviews for every implementation task. Create documents only when their phase starts.

tasks.title: Implement the game contracts and deterministic rules
tasks.details: Implement sections 4, 5, 7.1, and 8. Define strict choices, bounded decisions, immutable settings, outcomes, and legal state transitions. Implement pd-v1 scoring and all three versioned opponent policies with fixed branch explanations. Keep game code independent of transport, storage, provider, and telemetry libraries. Test every scoring entry, policy branch, boundary round, score total, draw, round-order rule, and terminal-state invariant.

tasks.title: Persist matches and expose replay data
tasks.details: Implement sections 8 and 9 using SQLite and ordered SQL migrations. Store required settings, observations, outcomes, attempts, timestamps, and trace references. Represent unknown usage and cost as null. Enforce unique round numbers and atomic outcome/progress commits. Use short transactions outside model requests. Reconstruct totals from stored outcomes. Provide replay reads without a browser or model calls. Document the storage decision and verify migrations, rollback, duplicate-round rejection, and replay consistency.

tasks.title: Prove ten-round execution with a fake player
tasks.details: Implement the application runner and fake player boundary. Build both observations before computing current decisions. Exclude current opponent choices and all stated reasons from player history. Opponents receive completed history without the visitor strategy. Reveal only committed outcomes. Failed rounds add no points, and partial matches have no winner. Verify reference totals of 30/30, 10/10, 50/0, 21/36, and 14/9. Record passing domain and persistence checks as the round 1 exit evidence.

tasks.title: Implement one bounded model adapter
tasks.details:
Implement sections 9.3, 10, and 15.5 with Pydantic AI. Select one provider and pin a supported model identifier using documented cost and structured-output evidence. Separate system rules from visitor strategy. Provide no model tools. Validate trimmed reasons of 1–240 characters and reject unknown fields. Enforce two requests per round across repair, transport, and SDK retries. Do not retry authentication or exhausted-budget errors. Record attempts, actual parameters, usage, estimated costs, and estimation basis. Add opt-in evaluation commands with bounded spending. Verify behavior offline and record model and retry decisions.

Review repair: Match settings can disagree with actual model execution
Round 2: Validate the stored provider, model, parameters, and system prompt version against the selected adapter before execution. Reject incompatible settings before issuing requests. Add boundary tests that prove completed records describe actual execution.
Evidence: An offline MockTransport workflow completed ten rounds with scores 30/30. Stored settings named different-model, max_completion_tokens=1, and different-system. Actual requests used gpt-6-luna and max_completion_tokens=256. The inconsistent replay read back successfully. application/runner.py does not compare settings with player/model.py constants.

tasks.title: Instrument execution and prepare reviewed trace sharing
tasks.details:
Implement section 11 trace scopes, attributes, stored references, and safe export failures. Include permitted model inputs, structured outputs, retries, policy branches, durations, scores, and available usage. Exclude credentials, source identifiers, access metadata, and unrelated request headers. Add an operator CLI to record or remove reviewed HTTPS links using an explicit Logfire host allowlist. Add executable trace checks and a full-trace review procedure. Prepare a public-access decision record covering plan limits, retention, supported sharing capabilities, and unverified questions. Do not infer an automatic sharing endpoint.

Review repair: Match tracing and reviewed-link management remain unimplemented
Round 2: Implement the required trace hierarchy, safe attributes, stored references, export-failure handling, and reviewed-link CLI. Prepare executable checks and the public-access decision record.
Evidence: application/runner.py contains no tracing scopes. The source inventory contains no telemetry module or reviewed-link CLI. README.md explicitly states that Logfire integration is unavailable.

tasks.title: Provide credentials and a bounded live-test allowance
tasks.details: External prerequisite for paid integration checks. Configure secrets outside the repository. Confirm access to the selected model and the Logfire project. The repository supplies no credentials or spending authorization. Local adapter, instrumentation, and review preparation remain autonomous tasks.

tasks.details:
Run one real, low-cost match within the approved allowance. Verify ten resolved rounds, actual model requests, and matching stored trace identifiers. Review every attribute against the public-record notice before publication. Record actual commands, costs, outcomes, plan settings, and any missing telemetry. Prepare exact supported-UI instructions for sharing, revocation, and replacement. Passing offline tests alone does not satisfy this task.

Create and verify a fresh reviewed link afterward. Store that link using the CLI. Record deployed results and applicable plan settings in the public-access decision record. This is the round 2 exit gate and must pass before visual polish or round 3 acceptance.

tasks.title: Implement match creation and progress endpoints
tasks.details: Implement section 12 with FastAPI and same-origin assets. Provide configuration, match creation, stored progress, replay routes, and safe health endpoints. Validate strategy length, opponent, current notice, acknowledgement, and optional existing parent. Use identifiers and idempotency keys with at least 128 bits of entropy. Persist acceptance before returning 202. Return specified 409, 422, 429, and 503 responses. Apply available execution limits without an unlimited queue. Serve only committed outcomes and safe error categories. Readiness performs no paid requests. Do not expose a visitor-match directory.

tasks.title: Build the complete play, replay, and rematch interface
tasks.details: Implement section 6 with the strategy field, three presets, three explained opponents, compact score matrix, acknowledgement, and Play ten rounds control. Presets only fill the field. Show waiting states, simultaneous committed choices, scores, timeline, and round details. Poll active matches once per second, reduce hidden-page polling, and stop at terminal states. Preserve progress across reloads. Render all supplied text as plain text. Show factual summaries, cooperation counts, combined score, copy link, and rematch controls. Distinguish own-match traces from named examples. Use verified span links only. Show partial failures honestly and explain interpretation limits.

Confirm examples and own-match Logfire links are distinguishable. Record evidence that a visitor can complete and understand a match without setup instructions. This is the round 3 exit gate.

tasks.title: Enforce persistent admission and spending limits
tasks.details: Complete sections 9, 12.2, and 13 admission safeguards. Enforce 24-hour idempotency with a unique key constraint and atomic concurrent duplicate handling. Apply four concurrent matches, three new matches per source per ten minutes, an 8 KiB body limit, 256 output tokens, 15-second requests, and a 180-second match deadline. Make specified limits configurable and document measured adjustments. Reserve worst-case model cost before acceptance using current verified prices. Persist reservations across restart, reset daily at 00:00 UTC, and retain conservative amounts for unknown charges. Configure a separate telemetry budget. Use trusted proxy configuration and short-lived source hashes outside replay and public telemetry.

Verify terminal states, safe errors, no fabricated outcomes, and unchanged stored scores after telemetry failure.

Include failed-match costs separately and preserve unknown-cost distinctions. Test event validation and report denominators. Document browser measurements as approximate. Do not equate clicks with activation or replay links with people.
